Based on the retrieved matches, it appears that residency selection criteria can predict performance in orthopaedic surgery residency. The study found that USMLE Step 2 scores, number of honors in medical school clerkships, and AOA (American Osteopathic Association) membership were significant predictors of resident performance.

In particular, these criteria helped the authors identify which factors may be "high yield" in ranking applicants for orthopaedic surgery residency programs. This suggests that the selection process has a tangible impact on the potential success of residents in this field.

While the study did not explore all possible sub-questions related to residency selection criteria, it provides evidence to support the idea that these factors can predict performance in orthopaedic surgery residency. The authors acknowledge that further research is needed to confirm their findings and explore the applicability of these results across different programs.
